findings.message: Prose has outgrown the links. A capability is a hub — move the detail into the documents it should be pointing at, and link to them from here.
missing required field 'frequency' (required when mechanism != not-enforced).

This control claims to run and does not say where the proof of it lives. Set `evidence` to the build log, the audit note or the dashboard — an unevidenced control is an assertion, and `not-enforced` is the honest value for one.
missing required field 'retention' (required when classification in [personal, special-category]).
This reads as an actual record rather than as a description of one. Addresses in examples belong under `example.com`, which RFC 2606 reserves so that it can never be anybody's.
This is longer than a capture should be. If it needs this much explaining it has outgrown the tier — promote it rather than expanding it here.
Prose has outgrown the links. Each fact restated here is a second copy to keep true — link to the document that owns it instead.
A bold RFC 2119 keyword binds, and an explanation does not. Move the obligation into a standard and link to it from here.
This carries more than one Symptom section, so it is more than one FAQ. Someone arriving with a symptom matches on the first one and never reads the second — split it.
'Branch' is out of order — it belongs before 'Item'.
The Failure modes section names no fallback. Say what happens instead when this fails, or say plainly that nothing does.
Something here reads as a credential rather than as a reference to one. Name the mechanism and where the value is held; never the value.
`measured-by` hedges rather than measures. Name the instrument and the number it reports — an NFR measured "where practical" is one nobody has to meet.
This claims a standing against a framework. A policy maps clauses to controls; where the organisation stands belongs in `frameworks.md`, the one place it can be kept true.
`detected-on` is before `occurred-on` — an incident cannot be found before it began. If the dates are right, the earlier one is when it started.
A step hedged with "typically", "usually" or "normally" leaves the reader to decide. Say what the ordering depends on, or state it plainly.
Symptoms must be the first section. Someone reaching for this at 2am matches on what they are seeing, not on what the document is called.
A standard cites where its authority comes from — an ADR in `derived-from`, a policy in `implements`, or both. With neither this is guidance, and guidance is an explanation.
This is deprecated and names no successor. Set `successor` to whatever took its place, so that someone arriving here from a manifest has somewhere to go next.
This is in trial and nothing says what would end the trial. Add a `## Trial criteria` section naming what is being evaluated, where, and what would settle it either way.
